title: Opinion, belief, conviction
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What is the difference between an opinion and a conviction?

I used a metaphor: an opinion is a table with about two legs, a belief has three and a conviction has four. As the legs stabilize, our emotional commitment grows from an opinion to a belief to a conviction.

A student summarized: what escalates it from one level to the next is questioning it, internally, analyzing and studying it. An opinion is something you heard on the way here. A belief is something you have heard repeatedly. Once it is a conviction, you do not allow anybody else's opinion to cloud your judgment.

I said: I do not think we should fear somebody changing our belief. When you get to convictions, I do not think you should be afraid of somebody questioning them. People should earn the right to question your conviction with intelligence.
A student said: welcome people questioning your convictions if they do it in a respectful, genuine manner, because it is easy to get entrenched, and as circumstances change you adapt.

I agreed but said it must not slow your decisions. There is a danger of paralysis by analysis. If you have a conviction, go with it until proven otherwise, but assume full responsibility and keep the pace.
Which of your opinions have you questioned enough to call a conviction?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you have done to question it.
Write who you would let question it.
Write how you will keep pace while you question.

check.q: What did I say a conviction has in my table metaphor?
What did a student say escalates an opinion to a conviction?
What did I say you must not do while you analyze?

recap: Question your opinions until they are convictions. Do not freeze while you do.
